task.title: Let the sidebar collapse to a rail
task.description:
Let the desktop shell's sidebar collapse to a narrow rail and expand again, so a board can take most of the window.

## Behavior

- Two widths. Expanded stays at 260px. Collapsed is a 76px rail, wide enough to keep the macOS traffic lights over shell chrome rather than over the board. The rail shows the menu button, the expand chevron, the import button as its plus glyph, and each project as a small tile carrying its status dot and key. Hovering a tile shows the full name and path.
- Toggle. A chevron button in the sidebar header beside the menu button, pointing left when expanded and right when collapsed. Cmd+B on macOS, Ctrl+B elsewhere.
- Remembered. The choice persists across restarts, stored beside the theme in the registry file.

## How it works

The main process owns the state, the same way it owns the theme, because it positions the board views: each board is a separate WebContentsView placed at the sidebar's width. The renderer asks for the current state at boot and invokes a toggle over a new channel. The main process saves the choice, repositions every board view to the new offset, and tells the shell, which sets a class on the root element that the stylesheet uses to draw the rail.

The shortcut lives in the main process too. When a board is showing, keyboard focus is inside that board's native view, so a listener in the shell page would never hear it. Each web view gets a before-input-event hook that recognizes the chord and toggles, so it works wherever focus is. No application menu is added.

## Files

- `desktop/src/main/main.js`: sidebar width becomes a function of the state, one new invoke channel, key hook on the chrome view and each board view.
- `desktop/src/main/registry.js`: a `sidebarCollapsed` field with getter and setter.
- `desktop/src/preload/preload.js`: the new invoke and change listener.
- `desktop/src/renderer/index.html`, `app.js`, `styles.css`: the chevron button, the root class, rail styles.
- `desktop/README.md`: one paragraph on the sidebar.

## Verification

The shell checks (`npm run check` in `desktop/`) catch a missing style rule, an unmatched element id, or an orphaned channel. Beyond that: run the app, toggle both ways with the button and the shortcut while a board is showing, restart to confirm the state is remembered, and put screenshots of both states in the PR.

Subagent-driven with per-task review and an adversarial whole-branch review; one fix wave. Verified by hand on macOS (screenshots attached): rail, both toggle paths, board repositioning, state round-trip. Not exercised: rail menu button, Windows/Linux.
